subject: System Design
title: The Ariane 5 Explosion
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Ariane 5 Explosion usable.

hook.text: On June 4, 1996, the Ariane 5 rocket exploded 37 seconds after launch, destroying $370 million in satellites.

buildup.text: Software from the Ariane 4 was reused in the Ariane 5. It had worked flawlessly for years.

discovery.text: A 64-bit floating point number was converted to a 16-bit integer. The Ariane 5's velocity exceeded the range.

twist.text: The code that crashed wasn't even needed during flight. It was a pre-launch calibration routine left running.

climax.text: An integer overflow in unnecessary code destroyed one of the most expensive rockets ever built.

punchline.text: An integer overflow blew up a $370 million rocket.

quiz.question: What caused the Ariane 5 explosion?
options: A 64-bit to 16-bit integer overflow in reused software
